claim.quote: A blind analysis has been performed. The data are consistent with the expected background in most of the explored energy range, and limits are set in previously unexplored regions of the available parameter space.

date.note: arXiv submission date (v1, 30 May 2025); published in JHEP 11 (2025) 007.

key_value_text.quote: The most significant deviation is found for s ≈ 16.90 MeV, corresponding to a global significance of approximately 2 standard deviations over the null hypothesis expectation.
key_value_text.value: Largest deviation at √s ≈ 16.90 MeV, a global significance of about 2 standard deviations; limits in previously unexplored parameter space

name: Search for a new 17 MeV resonance via e+e- annihilation with the PADME Experiment
notes: The abstract's deviation is not a claim of observation: the record's type is 'limit'.

summary.plain: PADME scanned its positron beam energy for a hypothetical 17 MeV particle, the X17, which could explain an anomaly in nuclear decays. The data match the expected background, new limits were set, and the largest excess is only about 2 standard deviations globally.
summary.technical: PADME at the DAΦNE linac (Run III): resonant e⁺e⁻ → X17 scan with 262 to 296 MeV positrons (√s 16.4 to 17.4 MeV), spacing below half the expected line width, below 1% uncertainty per energy point; blind analysis; consistent with background, limits in unexplored parameter space, largest deviation at √s ≈ 16.90 MeV with about 2σ global significance (JHEP 11 (2025) 007).

title: Search for a new 17 MeV resonance via e+e- annihilation with the PADME Experiment
why_it_matters: The abstract says the data are consistent with the background in most of the range, new limits are set, and the largest deviation is about 2 standard deviations globally.
